newsitem.title: USA: Oklahoma City memorial to include 168 chairs.
newsitem.headline: Oklahoma City memorial to include 168 chairs.

text.p: Oklahoma City bombing victims will be remembered with 168 stone-and-glass chairs in a memorial to be built on the site of the tragedy.
Officials said Tuesday they selected a memorial design by a German group that includes the empty chairs, each inscribed with the name of a victim, beside a shallow reflecting pond.
The memorial will cost $24.2 million and require two years to complete. Construction was expected to begin in December.

"It was our hope that the memorial design chosen would be the one that would most help the people of this community and this nation in overcoming the deep sense of loss," said Torrey Butzer, who along with husband Hans-Ekkehard Butzer and Sven Berg, created the design.
"Our focus was not on winning, but rather on simply reaching out to help like so many others around the world to offer a possible source of comfort and healing to those suffering," she said.
The design was chosen by a 15-member committee which reviewed 624 submissions over a year. The memorial will be funded mostly by private donations.

The Alfred P. Murrah federal building was destroyed in the April 19, 1995 blast that killed 168 people and injured hundreds of others. U.S. Army veteran Timothy McVeigh was convicted last month in the bombing and sentenced to death.
Since the blast, the building site has been cleared and surrounded by a chainlink fence while the memorial committee has sifted through the possible designs.
Nineteen of the memorial chairs will be smaller in size to commemorate the children who died in the blast, Butzer said.
